title: fast-labs-hosted-api-rapid-try-angles
content:
Objective:
Capture short, testable messaging and microcopy for a developer-first ‘try in 10 minutes’ flow for the Hosted API. Produce 3 distinct quickstart angles + 4 pricing anchor variants to A/B in marketing landing pages and SDK onboarding flows. Keep copy concise, engineering-toned, with clear success signals and low friction next steps.

Audience & constraints:
- Primary: backend/frontend engineers and ML engineers evaluating LLM APIs for production proofs-of-concept.
- Bridge to product managers/CTOs who sign up teams for paid plans.
- Must emphasize predictable latency, transparent cost, and seamless SDKs. Avoid heavy sales-y phrasing.
- Assume reader knows basics of LLMs but cares about integration effort and cost per inference.

Quickstart angles (3 high-level experiments)
1) Minimal Integration (5–10 min) — "Your first response, in a single file"
   - Hook: "Send a prompt. Get streaming text back. One SDK call."
   - Steps: 1) Sign up, 2) Install SDK (1 line), 3) Paste sample prompt, 4) Watch streamed tokens in terminal or browser.
   - Success metric: time-to-first-token (target < 5 min for 60% of signups).
   - Microcopy ideas: "Install, run, and see live tokens — no infra, no wait."
   - SDK snippet emphasis: single function, default model with latency-optimized routing.

2) Cost-first POC (20–30 min) — "Estimate unit economics as you build"
   - Hook: "Try the same prompt with three model tiers and see token/time/cost breakdown."
   - Steps: 1) Run prompt against 'latency' vs 'balanced' vs 'cost' profiles, 2) View per-call cost and latency in dashboard, 3) Enable lightweight caching (1 checkbox) to measure cost delta.
   - Success metric: % of users who check cost breakdown within session and create a cost alert.
   - Microcopy: "Preview token cost before you call — estimate and cap spend during prototyping."

3) Feature-to-Integration (45–60 min) — "Ship a small feature: summaries, chat, or classification"
   - Hook: "From playground to endpoint — shipping a feature that talks to your app in under an hour."
   - Steps: 1) Use sample app (Next.js/Flask) prewired with SDK, 2) Replace placeholder prompt with product prompt, 3) Deploy to preview.
   - Success metric: number of repos forked from quickstart and time to first full roundtrip test.
   - Microcopy: "Fork, customize, and call the new endpoint from your app — production-ready defaults included."

Developer-first value props (messaging frames)
- "Predictable latency, out-of-the-box": emphasize latency SLOs and latency-optimized model variants for interactive apps.
- "Transparent unit economics": show cost per token and per-call breakdowns in the quickstart to reduce billing surprise.
- "Same API across environments": highlight parity between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private to reduce vendor lock-in risk.
- "One-line SDKs, production defaults": shipping defaults (max_tokens, streaming enabled, batching heuristics) so engineers can iterate quickly without manual tuning.

Landing page microcopy variants (for A/B testing)
- Variant A (engineering neutral): "Get a streaming response in minutes. One SDK, one endpoint, predictable latency."
- Variant B (cost-focused): "Prototype with confidence — see per-request cost before you call."
- Variant C (ops-focused): "From hosted to private: same API, stronger controls for production."
- CTA permutations: "Try in 10 minutes" / "Run your first call" / "Estimate your cost"

Pricing-language drafts (4 anchor variants)
Note: language for landing/quickstart should be simple and avoid hard billing numbers in early copy; use examples in tooltips, docs, and pricing pages.
1) Pay-as-you-go anchor (developer default)
   - Headline: "Pay as you build — no upfront commit"
   - Microcopy: "Per-token billing with dev-friendly quotas. Start free, add a card later. Billing dashboard shows per-call breakdowns and usage alerts."
   - Tooltip example: "Example: A 500-token summary call ≈ ~0.5 units (see cost estimator)"

2) Starter monthly cap (recommended for teams)
   - Headline: "Starter plan: predictable baseline for small teams"
   - Microcopy: "Low monthly price guarantees baseline capacity and a discounted token rate for committed usage."
   - Messaging hook: "Great for teams that want predictable dev bills during POC."

3) Reserved throughput (mid-market pitch towards Dedicated)
   - Headline: "Reserve capacity for production SLAs"
   - Microcopy: "Monthly commitment for dedicated GPU pools, consistent latency, and priority support."
   - For quickstart: link to 'Need help sizing?' diagnostic tool.

4) Enterprise (compliance & private)
   - Headline: "Private deployments and compliance contracts"
   - Microcopy: "VPC, on-prem options, and audit integrations. Talk to sales for custom SLAs and pricing."

Risky phrasing to avoid
- "Cheapest" (signals low quality)
- Overpromising latency numbers without region/traffic context
- Highly technical kernel/quantization details in marketing copy — keep that in docs for later readers

Quick experiment matrix (what to A/B first)
- Variant axis: CTA phrasing / Price anchor / Quickstart angle / Hero microcopy
- Primary KPI: conversion to first API call (goal 25% uplift vs current baseline)
- Secondary KPIs: time-to-first-token, number of devs who view cost estimator, forked quickstart repos.

Example messaging flows for onboarding modal (concise, developer tone)
- Step 0 (signup success): "Welcome — one step left: install SDK and run your first call."
- Step 1 (post-install): "Run: rdw.call('hello world') — streaming enabled by default."
- Dashboard nudge: "Tip: Turn on cost preview to see per-call estimates before you send."

Telemetry & instrumentation we need for validation
- Track time from sign-up -> SDK install -> first token emitted.
- Flag which quickstart angle the user picked and whether they used cost estimator.
- Dashboard events: toggles for caching, routing policy, model tier chosen.
- Funnel: sign-up -> view quickstart -> run call -> enable billing -> add payment method.

Next steps (ops + content)
- Growth: implement 3 quickstart pages (one per angle) and wire to separate UTM funnels. 2-week sprint.
- Eng: add minimal SDK snippet variants (Python/Node/Go) to match 'minimal integration' flow. Priority: Node + Python.
- Product: build lightweight cost estimator widget (client-side) for quickstart pages.
- Analytics: instrument funnel events and create dashboard for first-token time and cost-estimator engagement.
- Legal: create brief blurb for sandbox limits and acceptable use on quickstart.

Appendix: copy snippets for in-product microcopy (short)
- Terminal success: "First token received — streaming live. Want lower latency? Switch to 'latency' profile."
- Cost preview label: "Estimated call cost: ~0.003 USD (based on 250 tokens)"
- Billing CTA: "Keep prototyping — set a cap to prevent surprise charges."

Notes to reviewers:
- Prioritize experiments that reduce time-to-first-token; that is our strongest immediate hook.
- Keep language developer-centric and avoid marketing fluff.
- We'll iterate with real developer sessions; collect quotes and friction points to refine copy.

End of brief.
